strengths: Strong rooted radial hazard concept with central toxic throat, basal mat, blisters, and spine halo supporting a clear stationary area-control read.
Articulatable part list separates crown, fronds, blister bank, spines, and root skirt well for swelling and spine-raise phases.
sourceGenerationRisks: Mixed anchors of coral, starfish, vent chimneys, and mats may generate a collage instead of one organism.
Perfect radial symmetry could flatten the sprite into an emblem and reduce readable hinge zones for fronds.
Corrosive brine cues risk becoming baked puddles, clouds, or environmental floor effects rather than riggable anatomy.

biologicalAnchors: Emphasize one mat-grown radial animal with vent-mineralized crown cup and blister sacs fused into the same basal tissue.
requiredRead: All rays, spines, and blisters must visibly grow from the low basal mat with no separate vent props.
promptRisks: Watch for coral reef decoration, detached chimney tubes, baked brine pools, and logo-like symmetry.
motionPhases: idle low mat with throat closed

referenceSearchTerms: hydrothermal vent microbial mat mineral crust

strengths: Coronate jellyfish anatomy gives a distinctive crown-lappet silhouette distinct from generic umbrella jellies.
Thick oral arms, four trailing tentacles, bead tips, and bell glow map cleanly to contraction, sweep, sting, and recoil animation.
sourceGenerationRisks: AI may default to a generic translucent umbrella jellyfish unless the deep groove and lappet crown are enforced.
Tentacles can become hair-like noise that is difficult to cut, weight, or read at sprite scale.
Bioluminescent alarm accents may become baked shock rings, bubbles, or water haze rather than anatomical glow overlays.

biologicalAnchors: Prioritize coronate jellyfish lappets and Atolla-like compact red-black bell over broad umbrella forms.
requiredRead: Deep bell groove, chunky crown rim, and separated oral arms must remain visible in the silhouette.
promptRisks: Avoid swarms, thin tentacle curtains, generic jellyfish bells, and baked sting flashes.

strengths: Megalodicopia-like tunicate anchor supports a rare sessile snap-trap read with a clear open siphon mouth.
Upper and lower siphon lobes, lip ridges, filter folds, stalk, and anchor foot provide practical hinge and squash articulation targets.
sourceGenerationRisks: The mouth-trap prompt may drift into clam, venus flytrap, or fantasy jaw anatomy, losing tunicate softness.
Translucency and internal organs can weaken the outer silhouette if rendered too faint.
Mucus strands, prey, or wall context could be baked into the source and interfere with cropping.

biologicalAnchors: Keep paired siphon lobes, gelatin tunic, and flexible stalk as the primary anatomy; use papillae instead of teeth.
requiredRead: Open siphon maw must be thick-lipped, soft, and connected to stalk and tunic body in one continuous organism.
promptRisks: Avoid hard teeth, plant leaves, clam shells, rock wall context, and faint transparent edges.

strengths: Rooted holdfast, central crown, gas bladders, and five to seven serrated blade-fronds give a strong sessile snare silhouette.
Broad blade-fronds and hinge knots are well suited to lane telegraphs, inward snap motion, and separate edge overlays.
sourceGenerationRisks: Kelp prompts can produce loose seaweed strips instead of one crop-safe organism with a central crown.
Thin fronds may read as spaghetti or tentacles and fail articulation at game scale.
Serrated edges and slash cues risk becoming baked motion trails or detached debris.

biologicalAnchors: Lean on bull kelp holdfast and gas bladder structure with broad ribbon kelp blades, not generic seaweed clumps.
requiredRead: Holdfast, crown node, hinge knots, and blade lanes must stay visible and connected as one ambusher.
promptRisks: Avoid detached strips, floating debris, hair-thin weed, baked slash trails, and overly plantlike harmless posture.

strengths: Central mouth pit, two thick petal-tentacle rings, lure bulbs, and buried column base make a clear lure ambusher with strong open/close readability.
Cerianthid and anemone anchors support retractable petal rings without needing mechanical teeth or gore.
sourceGenerationRisks: Flower language may produce a cute decorative bloom or coral cluster rather than a dangerous single predator.
Too many thin tentacles would be noisy and hard to articulate; rings need chunky separated petals.
Glow, sting sparks, halos, and digestive clouds may be baked into source art instead of kept as VFX.

biologicalAnchors: Emphasize sea anemone oral disc, tube anemone retraction, and corallimorph mushroom-anemone width with lure bulbs attached to tentacle tissue.
requiredRead: Central mouth depth and connected column base must remain visible even when petal rings are open.
promptRisks: Avoid land-plant leaves, literal teeth, decorative flowers, hair-thin tentacle crowds, and baked glow halos.
